   546→        spk_resh = interp_spk.reshape((nneu,-1))
   547→
   548→        # use odd trials to get dprime, using the raw frames activity instead of mean activity of each trial
   549→        stim1_fr = (ft_WallN == uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[0]]) & (ft_trInd % 2 == 0) & corr_fr # odd trials frames
   550→        stim2_fr = (ft_WallN == uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[1]]) & (ft_trInd % 2 == 0) & corr_fr # odd trials frames
   551→        grey_fr = (ft_trInd % 2==0) & grey_fr # odd trials gray frames
   552→        dp = dprime(spk[:, stim1_fr], spk[:, stim2_fr]) # get dprime 
   553→        # select neurons that response more in the texture area than in the gray space
   554→        corr_neu = (spk[:, stim1_fr].mean(1) > spk[:, grey_fr].mean(1)) | (spk[:, stim2_fr].mean(1) > spk[:, grey_fr].mean(1))
   555→
   556→        stim1_tr = WallN==uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[0]][0] # stim1 trials
   557→        stim2_tr = WallN==uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[1]][0] # stim2 trials
   558→
   559→        corr_spk = interp_spk[:, :, :40].copy() # get activity in the texture area 
   560→        u0 = interp_spk[:,:,42:52].reshape((nneu, -1)).mean(1, keepdims=1) # mean activity in gray space    
   561→        stim1_std = corr_spk[:, stim1_tr].reshape((nneu, -1)).std(1, keepdims=1) # std for stim1
   562→        stim2_std = corr_spk[:, stim2_tr].reshape((nneu, -1)).std(1, keepdims=1) # std for stim2    
   563→        # center to gray space, normalized by std of stim1 and stim2 
   564→        spk_norm = (2 * (spk_resh - u0) / (stim1_std + stim2_std)).reshape(interp_spk.shape)
   565→        # append activity from gray space of the previous trial 
   566→        gray_prev = np.empty((nneu, ntrials, n_bef)) * np.nan
   567→        gray_prev[:, 1:] = spk_norm[:, :-1, 60-n_bef:]
   568→        spk_norm = np.concatenate((gray_prev, spk_norm), axis=2) # concatenate the inter-trial-interval from previous trial    
   569→        print('done normalization..')
   570→        for i, iarn in enumerate(['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']): # ['V1','mHV','lHV','aHV']
   571→            thrs = np.percentile(dp[corr_neu & areas[i]], [100-prc, prc]) # get dprime value at percentile for corridor neurons and area    
   572→            stim1_idx = (dp >= thrs[0]) & corr_neu & areas[i]
   573→            stim2_idx = (dp <= thrs[1]) & corr_neu & areas[i]    
   574→            spk_proj_1[mname][iarn] = []
   575→            spk_proj_2[mname][iarn] = []
   576→
   577→            for j in range(7): #['circle1','circle2','leaf1','leaf2','leaf3','leaf1_swap1','leaf1_swap2']
   578→                if j in stim_ref:
   579→                    # only take even trials for stimuli whhich are used for getting the dprime

   581→                else:
   582→                    if np.sum(stim_id==j) > 0: # if stimulus is presented
   583→                        tr_idx = WallN == uniqW[stim_id == j]
   584→                    else:
   585→                        tr_idx = np.zeros(len(WallN)).astype(bool) 
   586→                spk_proj_1[mname][iarn].append(spk_norm[stim1_idx][:, tr_idx].mean(0)) # mean across neurons
   587→                spk_proj_2[mname][iarn].append(spk_norm[stim2_idx][:, tr_idx].mean(0)) # mean across neurons
   588→        print(n)

   591→    all_dat['proj_2_stim1'] = spk_proj_1

   705→def get_neuID_and_sortID(spk_in, max_pos=40):
   706→    """spk_in: neu * position"""
   707→    # get position index of peak activity inside corridor
   708→    maxind = np.argsort(spk_in[:, :max_pos], axis=1)[:, -1] 
   709→    sortID = np.argsort(maxind) # sort trials based on the peak positions
   710→    return sortID, maxind

   712→def get_stimNeu_and_sorted(db, beh, stim_ref=[2, 0], thr=0.3, root='', load_save_interp_spk=1):
   713→    all_stim = ['circle1','circle2','leaf1','leaf2','leaf3','leaf1_swap1','leaf1_swap2']
   714→    spk = load_spk(db, root=os.path.join(root, 'spk'))

   716→    neu,nfr = spk.shape

   718→    ft_trInd = beh['ft_trInd'][:nfr]
   719→    ft_WallN = beh['ft_WallID'][:nfr]    
   720→    VRmove = beh['ft_move'][:nfr]>0
   721→    corr_fr = beh['ft_CorrSpc'][:nfr] & VRmove    
   722→    trInd = np.arange(ntrials)
   723→    # use odd trials (training trials) to get dprime, using the raw frames activity 
   724→    stim1_train_fr = (ft_WallN == uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[0]]) & (ft_trInd%2 == 0) & corr_fr # odd trials frames
   725→    stim2_train_fr = (ft_WallN == uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[1]]) & (ft_trInd%2 == 0) & corr_fr # odd trials frames
   726→    dp = dprime(spk[:, stim1_train_fr], spk[:, stim2_train_fr]) # get dprime

   733→        ft_AcumPos = beh['ft_PosCum'][:nfr]
   734→        interp_spk = get_interpPos_spk(spk[:, VRmove], ft_AcumPos[VRmove], 
   735→                                             ntrials, n_bins=60, lengths=CL)    
   736→    print('done loading interpolated spk..')
   737→    # take test trials of selective neurons for sorting

   739→    stim1_test_tr = (WallN==uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[0]])[test_tr]
   740→    stim2_test_tr = (WallN==uniqW[stim_id==stim_ref[1]])[test_tr]

   743→    
   744→    gray_u = test_spk[:, :, 40:].reshape((neu,-1)).mean(1,keepdims=1) # get mean of gray space
   745→    norm_spk = test_spk.reshape((neu, -1))

   748→    stim1_neu = norm_spk[dp>=thr] # get spk for stimulus 1 selective neurons
   749→    stim2_neu = norm_spk[dp<=-thr] # get spk for stimulus 2 selective neurons

   772→

   777→def get_seq_corr(dat, stim_sort='leaf1'):

   814→def get_kfold_reward_response(root, db, Beh):
   815→    dat = {}
   816→    for ndb in db:
   817→        aHV = load_retino(ndb, root = os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy'))['neu_ar_idx']['aHV']
   818→        mHV = load_retino(ndb, root = os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy'))['neu_ar_idx']['mHV']
   819→        spk = load_spk(ndb, root=os.path.join(root, 'spk'))
   820→        spk = stats.zscore(spk, axis=1)
   821→        interp_spk = load_interp_spk(ndb, root=os.path.join(root, 'process_data'))
   822→        u_spk = interp_spk[:, :, 5:40].mean(2) # take mean activity within texture area, starting from 5 (0.5 meter)
   823→        spk0 = stats.zscore(interp_spk.reshape(interp_spk.shape[0], -1), axis=1).reshape(interp_spk.shape)
   824→        
   825→        if 'stimtype' in ndb.keys():
   826→            beh = Beh['%s_%s_%s_%s'%(ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk'], ndb['stimtype'])]
   827→            mname = ndb['mname'] + '_' + ndb['stimtype']
   828→        else:
   829→            beh = Beh['%s_%s_%s'%(ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk'])]
   830→            mname = ndb['mname']
   831→        SoundFr = beh['SoundFr'].astype(int)
   832→        Pos = np.mod(beh['SoundDelPos'], beh['Corridor_Length']) # reward positions and cue positions are highly correlated in reward corridor
   833→                                                                   # since non-reward corridor doesn't have reward, so we use cue positions instead
   834→        u_pos = Pos.mean()
   835→        if any(Pos<0):
   836→            print('some cue frame index are nagtive')
   837→        uniqW, WallN, isRew, ntrials = beh['UniqWalls'], beh['WallName'], beh['isRew'], beh['ntrials']
   838→        stim_id = beh['stim_id']
   839→        stim1 = WallN==uniqW[stim_id==2]
   840→        stim2 = WallN==uniqW[stim_id==0]
   841→
   842→        resp = np.empty(interp_spk.shape[1:])
   843→        stim_resp = np.empty(interp_spk.shape[1:])
   844→
   845→        ranges = np.array([15, 15])
   846→        spk2Flick = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   847→        lick2Flick = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   848→        Flick_pos = np.empty(ntrials) * np.nan
   849→        spk2Cue = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   850→        lick2Cue = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   851→        
   852→        random.seed(2025)
   853→        tr_shuf = np.random.permutation(ntrials)
   854→        nfold = 10
   855→        k_tr = int(np.ceil(beh['ntrials']/nfold))
   856→        for k in range(nfold): # 10 folds
   857→            test_tr = np.zeros(ntrials).astype(bool)
   858→            test_tr[tr_shuf[k * k_tr : (k+1) * k_tr]] = True # test trials index
   859→            ### using training trials to get dprimes
   860→            dp0 = dprime(spk[:, SoundFr[stim1 & ~test_tr]], spk[:, SoundFr[stim2 & ~test_tr]]) # equivilent to using all frames within the whole corridor
   861→            dp1 = dprime(u_spk[:, (Pos > u_pos) & stim1 & ~test_tr & isRew],
   862→                              u_spk[:, (Pos <= u_pos) & stim1 & ~test_tr & isRew])        
   863→            thr = np.percentile(dp1[aHV], 95) # dprime at 95 percentile in aHV
   864→            sel_idx = (dp0 > 0.3) & (dp1 >= thr) & aHV
   865→
   866→            sel_spk = spk0[sel_idx, :, :][:, test_tr]
   867→            resp[test_tr] = np.nanmean(sel_spk, 0) # mean across neurons
   868→            
   869→            stim_resp[test_tr] = spk0[(dp0 >= 0.3) & mHV][:, test_tr].mean(0) # get leaf1 selective neurons from mHV 
   870→            print('%d fold, neurons selected: %d'%(k, sel_idx.sum()))
   871→
   872→            Flick_pos_temp, spk2Flick_temp, lick2Flick_temp = spk_2_firstLick(spk[sel_idx].mean(0), beh, ranges=ranges, bins=30)

   882→    return dat

   884→def get_reward_neuorns(root, db, beh):
   885→    dat = {}
   886→
   887→    aHV = load_retino(db, root = os.path.join(root, 'retinotopy'))['neu_ar_idx']['aHV']
   888→    spk = load_spk(db, root=os.path.join(root, 'spk'))
   889→    interp_spk = load_interp_spk(db, root=os.path.join(root, 'process_data'))
   890→    u_spk = interp_spk[:, :, 5:40].mean(2) # take mean activity within texture area, starting from 5 (0.5 meter)
   891→    spk0 = stats.zscore(interp_spk.reshape(interp_spk.shape[0], -1), axis=1).reshape(interp_spk.shape)
   892→
   893→    SoundFr = beh['SoundFr'].astype(int)

   896→    u_pos = Pos.mean()

   898→    stim_id = beh['stim_id']
   899→    stim1 = WallN==uniqW[stim_id==2]

   901→
   902→    dp0 = dprime(spk[:, SoundFr[stim1]], spk[:, SoundFr[stim2]]) # equivilent to using all frames within the whole corridor
   903→    dp1 = dprime(u_spk[:, (Pos >= u_pos) & stim1 & isRew], u_spk[:, (Pos < u_pos) & stim1 & isRew])        
   904→    thr = np.percentile(dp1[aHV], 95) # dprime at 95 percentile in aHV
   905→    sel_idx = (dp0 >= 0.3) & (dp1 >= thr) & aHV
   906→

   913→def spk_2_firstLick(spk, beh, ranges=[15, 15], bins=30):
   914→    """ranges: frames included before and after first lick
   915→        spk: one dimensional activity
   916→    """
   917→    lickPos, lickFr, lickTr, ntrials  = beh['LickPos'], beh['LickFr'].astype(int), beh['LickTrind'].astype(int), beh['ntrials']
   918→    spk2Flick = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   919→    lick2Flick = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   920→    Flick_pos = np.empty(ntrials) * np.nan
   921→    for n in range(ntrials):
   922→        idx = lickTr==n
   923→        if idx.sum()>0:
   924→            F_id = int(lickFr[np.where(idx)[0][0]]) # first lick frame index
   925→            lickFr_offset = lickFr - F_id # align lick frame to first lick
   926→            temp_spk = spk[F_id - ranges[0] : F_id+ranges[1]]
   927→            if len(temp_spk)>0:
   928→                Flick_pos[n] = lickPos[idx][0]
   929→                spk2Flick[n] = spk[F_id - ranges[0] : F_id+ranges[1]]
   930→                temp_lick = lickFr_offset[(lickFr_offset>=-ranges[0]) & (lickFr_offset<=ranges[1])] + ranges[0]
   931→                hist, edge = np.histogram(temp_lick, bins=bins, range=(0, np.sum(ranges)))
   932→                lick2Flick[n] = hist
   933→    return Flick_pos, spk2Flick, lick2Flick

   935→def spk_2_cue(spk, beh, ranges=[15, 15], bins=30):
   936→    """ranges: frames included before and after cue frame
   937→        spk: one dimensional activity
   938→    """
   939→    SoundFr, lickFr, lickTr, ntrials  = beh['SoundFr'].astype(int), beh['LickFr'].astype(int), beh['LickTrind'].astype(int), beh['ntrials']
   940→    spk2Cue = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   941→    lick2Cue = np.empty((ntrials, np.sum(ranges))) * np.nan
   942→    for n in range(ntrials):
   943→        spk2Cue[n] = spk[SoundFr[n] - ranges[0] : SoundFr[n] + ranges[1]]
   944→        
   945→        temp_lick = lickFr[(lickFr>=SoundFr[n]-ranges[0]) & (lickFr<=SoundFr[n]+ranges[1])] - SoundFr[n] + ranges[0]
   946→        hist, edge = np.histogram(temp_lick, bins=bins, range=(0, np.sum(ranges)))
   947→        lick2Cue[n] = hist
   948→    return spk2Cue, lick2Cue

<cell id="7d526335"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Definition of variables in Behavior data</cell id="7d526335">
<cell id="005314c3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>Calcium signal recording frame rate: fs = 3.17Hz

Variables inside beh:
*    beh['ntrials']: number of trials
*    beh['trInd']: trials index
*    beh['trInd_odd']: the index of odd trials
*    beh['trInd_even']: the index of even trials
*   beh['Trial_start_time']: time when animal enters each corridor
*    beh['Trial_end_time']: time when animal ran out each corridor
*    beh['stim_id']: ID of stimuli; 0:circle1, 1:circle2, 2:leaf1, 3:leaf2 4:leaf3, 5:leaf1_swap1, 6:leaf1_swap2
*    beh['SubjMove']: running information
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMTime']: time stamps of running
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPos']: position inside corridor
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum']: cumulative position inside VR
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMDistCum']: almost identical with beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum']
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch']: pitch (forward) running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_roll']: roll direction running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_yaw']: yaw direction running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch_cum']: total running distance. Note that it is not the same as beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum'] given that we only move the VR and with a constant speed when beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch'] pass a threshold
*    beh['Gray_space_time']: time when animal entered the gray space
*    beh['SoundPos']: position of sound cue
*    beh['SoundTime']: time of sound cue
*    beh['SoundTimeDelay']: time of sound cue with a delay, if delay=0, then it is the same as beh['SoundTime']
*    beh['RewTime']: time of reward delivery, these numbers only valid in the reward corridor.
*    beh['RewPos']: position of reward delivery, with NaN in the non-reward corridor.
*    beh['isRew']: boolean value indicating if the trial is a reward trial.
*    beh['WallType']: category of stimuli, but please ignore this one since it doesn't apply to our experiments
*    beh['WallIsProbe']: whether is a catch trial, but please ignore this one
*    beh['WallName']: name of stimuli in each corridor
*    beh['UniqWalls']: name of stimuli in the whole session
*    beh['LickTrind']: trial stamp of each lick
*    beh['LickTime']: time stamp of each lick
*    beh['LickPos']: positional stamp of each lick
*    beh['Lick_wallName']: corresponding stimulus of each lick
*    beh['VRpos']: position inside VR
*    beh['VRposCum']: cumulative position inside VR
*    beh['VRposTime']: time stamp for beh['VRpos'] and beh['VRposCum']
*    beh['ft']: time stamp for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_trInd']: trial stamp for each neural frame, NaN means outside the behavior recorded
*    beh['ft_trInd_odd']: neural frames from odd trials
*    beh['ft_trInd_even']: neural frames from even trials
*    beh['ft_Pos']: position inside VR for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_PosCum']: culculative position inside VR for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_move']: the differences between each frame of beh['ft_PosCum']
*    beh['ft_isMoving']: boolean value for beh['ft_move']>0
*    beh['ft_GraySpc']: boolean value indicating if animals is inside gray space
*    beh['ft_CorrSpc']: boolean value indicating if animals is inside texture area
*    beh['ft_WallID']: the corridor each neural frame belongs to
*    beh['ft_RunCum']: cumulative running distance for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_RunSpeed']: running speed for each neural frame
*    beh['RunFr']: same as beh['ft_RunSpeed']
*    beh['run_pos']: running speed interpolated into trials * positions
*    beh['RewardFr']: neural frame when reward was delivered, length=ntrials, NaN means trial without reward being delivered
*    beh['StartFr']: neural frame when animal enter each corridor
*    beh['GrayFr']: neural frame when animal enter gray space
*    beh['EndFr']: neural frame when animal ran out of a corridor
*    beh['LickFr']: neural frame when animal licked
*    beh['SoundFr']: neural frame when cound cue was delivered
*    beh['SoundDelayFr']: neural frame when cound cue was delivered + a delay, if delay=0, then it is the same as beh['SoundFr']
*    beh['SoundDelPos']: position inside a corridor, corresponding to beh['SoundDelayFr']
*    beh['BefCueFr']: boolean values indicating neural frames after entered corridor but before cue was delivered
*    beh['AftCueFr']: boolean values indicating neural frames after cue was delivered
*    beh['TrialStim']: stimulus name of each trial
*    beh['StimTrial']: subfields are trial index of each stimulus
*    beh['StimFrame']: subfields are neural frame index of each stimulus

Below are some settings:

*    beh['Corridor_Length']: length of the corridor
*    beh['Gray_Space_length']: length of gray space
*    beh['Texture_Length']: length of texture area
*    beh['Reward_Mode']: reward mode of experiment, either passive reward in which reward was delivered without lick or active reward in which reward was triggered be licking
*    beh['Reward_Delay_ms']: delay time for reward, this is a setting. Find the actually reward time in beh['RewTime']</cell id="005314c3">

### Make sure there is at least 1320 GB empty space (420GB for raw data + 900GB for processed data)

# there are two options to download the data 
# (1) Download all data as a zip file from the Figshare website, we found this is much faster.

#     but since it downloads indvidual file, you can resume it if got interupted and it will download the remaining files.

# utils.download_data_from_figshare(root)
## Definition of variables in Behavior data

Calcium signal recording frame rate: fs = 3.17Hz

Variables inside beh:
*    beh['ntrials']: number of trials
*    beh['trInd']: trials index
*    beh['trInd_odd']: the index of odd trials
*    beh['trInd_even']: the index of even trials
*   beh['Trial_start_time']: time when animal enters each corridor
*    beh['Trial_end_time']: time when animal ran out each corridor
*    beh['stim_id']: ID of stimuli; 0:circle1, 1:circle2, 2:leaf1, 3:leaf2 4:leaf3, 5:leaf1_swap1, 6:leaf1_swap2
*    beh['SubjMove']: running information
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMTime']: time stamps of running

import os
import utils
import numpy as np
import time

# Download all data from Figshare
### Make sure there is at least 1320 GB empty space (420GB for raw data + 900GB for processed data)

# there are two options to download the data 
# (1) Download all data as a zip file from the Figshare website, we found this is much faster. 
#     link: https://doi.org/10.25378/janelia.28811129.v1
#     however, it might get interupted if the internet is disconnected. 
#     Make sure to change the 'root' below to the folder where the data is
# (2) Another way is to download via Figshare API (uncomment the last line in this cell). We found it takes a bit longer time,
#     but since it downloads indvidual file, you can resume it if got interupted and it will download the remaining files.

root = r'E:\Zhong-et-2025' # modify this to be your local folders

# utils.download_data_from_figshare(root)
## Definition of variables in Behavior data

Calcium signal recording frame rate: fs = 3.17Hz

Variables inside beh:
*    beh['ntrials']: number of trials
*    beh['trInd']: trials index
*    beh['trInd_odd']: the index of odd trials
*    beh['trInd_even']: the index of even trials
*   beh['Trial_start_time']: time when animal enters each corridor
*    beh['Trial_end_time']: time when animal ran out each corridor
*    beh['stim_id']: ID of stimuli; 0:circle1, 1:circle2, 2:leaf1, 3:leaf2 4:leaf3, 5:leaf1_swap1, 6:leaf1_swap2
*    beh['SubjMove']: running information
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMTime']: time stamps of running
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPos']: position inside corridor
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum']: cumulative position inside VR
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMDistCum']: almost identical with beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum']
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch']: pitch (forward) running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_roll']: roll direction running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_yaw']: yaw direction running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch_cum']: total running distance. Note that it is not the same as beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum'] given that we only move the VR and with a constant speed when beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch'] pass a threshold
*    beh['Gray_space_time']: time when animal entered the gray space
*    beh['SoundPos']: position of sound cue
*    beh['SoundTime']: time of sound cue
*    beh['SoundTimeDelay']: time of sound cue with a delay, if delay=0, then it is the same as beh['SoundTime']
*    beh['RewTime']: time of reward delivery, these numbers only valid in the reward corridor.
*    beh['RewPos']: position of reward delivery, with NaN in the non-reward corridor.
*    beh['isRew']: boolean value indicating if the trial is a reward trial.
*    beh['WallType']: category of stimuli, but please ignore this one since it doesn't apply to our experiments
*    beh['WallIsProbe']: whether is a catch trial, but please ignore this one
*    beh['WallName']: name of stimuli in each corridor
*    beh['UniqWalls']: name of stimuli in the whole session
*    beh['LickTrind']: trial stamp of each lick
*    beh['LickTime']: time stamp of each lick
*    beh['LickPos']: positional stamp of each lick
*    beh['Lick_wallName']: corresponding stimulus of each lick
*    beh['VRpos']: position inside VR
*    beh['VRposCum']: cumulative position inside VR
*    beh['VRposTime']: time stamp for beh['VRpos'] and beh['VRposCum']
*    beh['ft']: time stamp for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_trInd']: trial stamp for each neural frame, NaN means outside the behavior recorded
*    beh['ft_trInd_odd']: neural frames from odd trials
*    beh['ft_trInd_even']: neural frames from even trials
*    beh['ft_Pos']: position inside VR for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_PosCum']: culculative position inside VR for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_move']: the differences between each frame of beh['ft_PosCum']
*    beh['ft_isMoving']: boolean value for beh['ft_move']>0
*    beh['ft_GraySpc']: boolean value indicating if animals is inside gray space
*    beh['ft_CorrSpc']: boolean value indicating if animals is inside texture area
*    beh['ft_WallID']: the corridor each neural frame belongs to
*    beh['ft_RunCum']: cumulative running distance for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_RunSpeed']: running speed for each neural frame
*    beh['RunFr']: same as beh['ft_RunSpeed']
*    beh['run_pos']: running speed interpolated into trials * positions
*    beh['RewardFr']: neural frame when reward was delivered, length=ntrials, NaN means trial without reward being delivered
*    beh['StartFr']: neural frame when animal enter each corridor
*    beh['GrayFr']: neural frame when animal enter gray space
*    beh['EndFr']: neural frame when animal ran out of a corridor
*    beh['LickFr']: neural frame when animal licked
*    beh['SoundFr']: neural frame when cound cue was delivered
*    beh['SoundDelayFr']: neural frame when cound cue was delivered + a delay, if delay=0, then it is the same as beh['SoundFr']
*    beh['SoundDelPos']: position inside a corridor, corresponding to beh['SoundDelayFr']
*    beh['BefCueFr']: boolean values indicating neural frames after entered corridor but before cue was delivered
*    beh['AftCueFr']: boolean values indicating neural frames after cue was delivered
*    beh['TrialStim']: stimulus name of each trial
*    beh['StimTrial']: subfields are trial index of each stimulus
*    beh['StimFrame']: subfields are neural frame index of each stimulus

Below are some settings:

*    beh['Corridor_Length']: length of the corridor
*    beh['Gray_Space_length']: length of gray space
*    beh['Texture_Length']: length of texture area
*    beh['Reward_Mode']: reward mode of experiment, either passive reward in which reward was delivered without lick or active reward in which reward was triggered be licking
*    beh['Reward_Delay_ms']: delay time for reward, this is a setting. Find the actually reward time in beh['RewTime']

## Data process
### takes about 8 hours

# load experiment information for imaging mice
exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(root, r'beh\Imaging_Exp_info.npy'), allow_pickle=1).item()
exp_info.keys()

    os.makedirs(proc_root)

# get interpolational neural activity (neurons * trials * positions)
# bins of positon: 60, each bin is 1 decimeter, total length of corridor is 6 meters

    print(exp_type)

        if os.path.exists(save_name):
            print("File has been created")
        else:    
            beh = Beh[kn]
            spk = utils.load_spk(ndb, root=os.path.join(root, 'spk'))
            nneu, nfr = spk.shape  

            ntrials, CL = beh['ntrials'], beh['Corridor_Length']    
            VRmove = beh['ft_move'][:nfr]>0
            ft_AcumPos = beh['ft_PosCum'][:nfr]

            utils.get_interpPos_spk(spk[:, VRmove], ft_AcumPos[VRmove], ntrials, n_bins=60, 
                                    lengths=CL, save_path=save_name)

    # save the dprime

    np.save(os.path.join(root, 'process_data', fn), all_dat)
    print(fn)

<cell id="7d526335"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>## Definition of variables in Behavior data</cell id="7d526335">
<cell id="005314c3"><cell_type>markdown</cell_type>Calcium signal recording frame rate: fs = 3.17Hz

Variables inside beh:
*    beh['ntrials']: number of trials
*    beh['trInd']: trials index
*    beh['trInd_odd']: the index of odd trials
*    beh['trInd_even']: the index of even trials
*   beh['Trial_start_time']: time when animal enters each corridor
*    beh['Trial_end_time']: time when animal ran out each corridor
*    beh['stim_id']: ID of stimuli; 0:circle1, 1:circle2, 2:leaf1, 3:leaf2 4:leaf3, 5:leaf1_swap1, 6:leaf1_swap2
*    beh['SubjMove']: running information
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMTime']: time stamps of running
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPos']: position inside corridor
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum']: cumulative position inside VR
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjMDistCum']: almost identical with beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum']
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch']: pitch (forward) running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_roll']: roll direction running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_yaw']: yaw direction running speed
*    beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch_cum']: total running distance. Note that it is not the same as beh['SubjMove']['SubjMPosCum'] given that we only move the VR and with a constant speed when beh['SubjMove']['SubjM_pitch'] pass a threshold
*    beh['Gray_space_time']: time when animal entered the gray space
*    beh['SoundPos']: position of sound cue
*    beh['SoundTime']: time of sound cue
*    beh['SoundTimeDelay']: time of sound cue with a delay, if delay=0, then it is the same as beh['SoundTime']
*    beh['RewTime']: time of reward delivery, these numbers only valid in the reward corridor.
*    beh['RewPos']: position of reward delivery, with NaN in the non-reward corridor.
*    beh['isRew']: boolean value indicating if the trial is a reward trial.
*    beh['WallType']: category of stimuli, but please ignore this one since it doesn't apply to our experiments
*    beh['WallIsProbe']: whether is a catch trial, but please ignore this one
*    beh['WallName']: name of stimuli in each corridor
*    beh['UniqWalls']: name of stimuli in the whole session
*    beh['LickTrind']: trial stamp of each lick
*    beh['LickTime']: time stamp of each lick
*    beh['LickPos']: positional stamp of each lick
*    beh['Lick_wallName']: corresponding stimulus of each lick
*    beh['VRpos']: position inside VR
*    beh['VRposCum']: cumulative position inside VR
*    beh['VRposTime']: time stamp for beh['VRpos'] and beh['VRposCum']
*    beh['ft']: time stamp for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_trInd']: trial stamp for each neural frame, NaN means outside the behavior recorded
*    beh['ft_trInd_odd']: neural frames from odd trials
*    beh['ft_trInd_even']: neural frames from even trials
*    beh['ft_Pos']: position inside VR for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_PosCum']: culculative position inside VR for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_move']: the differences between each frame of beh['ft_PosCum']
*    beh['ft_isMoving']: boolean value for beh['ft_move']>0
*    beh['ft_GraySpc']: boolean value indicating if animals is inside gray space
*    beh['ft_CorrSpc']: boolean value indicating if animals is inside texture area
*    beh['ft_WallID']: the corridor each neural frame belongs to
*    beh['ft_RunCum']: cumulative running distance for each neural frame
*    beh['ft_RunSpeed']: running speed for each neural frame
*    beh['RunFr']: same as beh['ft_RunSpeed']
*    beh['run_pos']: running speed interpolated into trials * positions
*    beh['RewardFr']: neural frame when reward was delivered, length=ntrials, NaN means trial without reward being delivered
*    beh['StartFr']: neural frame when animal enter each corridor
*    beh['GrayFr']: neural frame when animal enter gray space
*    beh['EndFr']: neural frame when animal ran out of a corridor
*    beh['LickFr']: neural frame when animal licked
*    beh['SoundFr']: neural frame when cound cue was delivered
*    beh['SoundDelayFr']: neural frame when cound cue was delivered + a delay, if delay=0, then it is the same as beh['SoundFr']
*    beh['SoundDelPos']: position inside a corridor, corresponding to beh['SoundDelayFr']
*    beh['BefCueFr']: boolean values indicating neural frames after entered corridor but before cue was delivered
*    beh['AftCueFr']: boolean values indicating neural frames after cue was delivered
*    beh['TrialStim']: stimulus name of each trial
*    beh['StimTrial']: subfields are trial index of each stimulus
*    beh['StimFrame']: subfields are neural frame index of each stimulus

Below are some settings:

*    beh['Corridor_Length']: length of the corridor
*    beh['Gray_Space_length']: length of gray space
*    beh['Texture_Length']: length of texture area
*    beh['Reward_Mode']: reward mode of experiment, either passive reward in which reward was delivered without lick or active reward in which reward was triggered be licking
*    beh['Reward_Delay_ms']: delay time for reward, this is a setting. Find the actually reward time in beh['RewTime']</cell id="005314c3">

Since reward availability and day-of-training only make sense for task/supervised mice, I'm narrowing down to sessions from that cohort that have all the necessary variables (sound cue timing, training day, trial structure) needed for the decoder, rather than including unsupervised, naive, or grating sessions.

I realize the decoder needs time-aligned neural activity per trial rather than the paper's position-interpolated format, so I need to work directly with the deconvolved fluorescence traces aligned to corridor entry, using the imaging frame rate of about 3.17 Hz to compute frame-to-time conversion. Since trial durations vary with running speed, I need to figure out how to handle variable-length trials when aligning to corridor entry and exit frames.

Actually the task specifies temporal alignment based on trial start, not position-based binning. But since VR moves at constant speed while running, position-interpolated bins effectively serve as a consistent time axis too — 60 bins per trial across the 6m corridor at 0.1m resolution gives uniform trial lengths, which resolves the variable-duration issue from stop/start running.

But then I realize the decoder actually needs distinct feature types: time-to-cue and time-since-start require true elapsed time, whereas corridor position and running speed are separate variables that shouldn't be conflated with time bins.

I think the cleanest solution is to use raw frame-by-frame neural data aligned to trial start, with each frame acting as a time bin at the native sampling rate—this keeps time bins genuinely uniform while letting all the behavioral variables be computed naturally within them. python3 -c "
import numpy as np
import os

DATA_ROOT = '/app/data'
exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'beh', 'Imaging_Exp_info.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()

# Collect unique sessions
unique_sessions = {}
for exp_type, db_list in exp_info.items():
    for ndb in db_list:
        key = (ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk'])
        if key not in unique_sessions:
            unique_sessions[key] = {'exp_types': [exp_type], 'ndb': ndb}
        else:
            unique_sessions[key]['exp_types'].append(exp_type)

print(f'Total unique sessions: {len(unique_sessions)}')

# Check which sessions have spk files
spk_files = set(f.replace('_neural_data.npy','') for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'spk')))
retino_files = set(f.replace('_trans.npz','') for f in os.listdir(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'retinotopy')))

matched = 0
for key, info in unique_sessions.items():
    mname, datexp, blk = key
    spk_key = f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}'
    ret_key = f'{mname}_{datexp}'
    has_spk = spk_key in spk_files
    has_ret = ret_key in retino_files
    if has_spk and has_ret:
        matched += 1
    else:
        print(f'MISSING: {spk_key} spk={has_spk} ret={has_ret} exp_types={info[\"exp_types\"]}')

print(f'Sessions with both spk and retinotopy: {matched}')

# List unique mice
mice = set()
for key in unique_sessions:
    mice.add(key[0])
print(f'Unique mice: {sorted(mice)}')
print(f'Number of unique mice: {len(mice)}')
"

arguments.command:
python3 -c "
import numpy as np
import os

DATA_ROOT = '/app/data'
exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'beh', 'Imaging_Exp_info.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()

# Check a few sessions for data sizes and key behavioral variables
test_sessions = [
    ('sup_train1_after_learning', 0),  # supervised, after learning
    ('unsup_test1', 0),  # unsupervised test
    ('naive_test1', 0),  # naive test
]

for exp_type, idx in test_sessions:
    ndb = exp_info[exp_type][idx]
    mname, datexp, blk = ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk']
    print(f'\\n=== {exp_type}: {mname}_{datexp}_{blk} ===')
    
    # Load spk
    spk_data = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'spk', f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_neural_data.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()
    n_neurons = sum(s.shape[0] for s in spk_data['spks'])
    n_frames = spk_data['spks'][0].shape[1]
    print(f'Neurons: {n_neurons}, Frames: {n_frames}, Planes: {len(spk_data[\"spks\"])}')
    
    # Load retinotopy
    ret = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'retinotopy', f'{mname}_{datexp}_trans.npz'), allow_pickle=True)
    iarea = ret['iarea']
    print(f'Retinotopy iarea: {len(iarea)} neurons')
    unique, counts = np.unique(iarea, return_counts=True)
    print(f'  Area distribution: {dict(zip(unique.astype(int), counts))}')
    vc_count = np.sum((iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7))
    print(f'  Visual cortex neurons (excl -1, 7): {vc_count} ({100*vc_count/len(iarea):.1f}%)')
    
    # Load behavior
    Beh = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'beh', f'Beh_{exp_type}.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()
    if 'stimtype' in ndb:
        beh_key = f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_{ndb[\"stimtype\"]}'
    else:
        beh_key = f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}'
    beh = Beh[beh_key]
    
    print(f'Trials: {beh[\"ntrials\"]}')
    print(f'Corridor_Length: {beh[\"Corridor_Length\"]}')
    print(f'Texture_Length: {beh[\"Texture_Length\"]}')
    print(f'UniqWalls: {beh[\"UniqWalls\"]}')
    print(f'SoundPos range: [{beh[\"SoundPos\"].min():.1f}, {beh[\"SoundPos\"].max():.1f}]')
    print(f'isRew sum: {beh[\"isRew\"].sum()}/{beh[\"ntrials\"]}')
    print(f'StartFr range: [{np.nanmin(beh[\"StartFr\"]):.0f}, {np.nanmax(beh[\"StartFr\"]):.0f}]')
    print(f'GrayFr range: [{np.nanmin(beh[\"GrayFr\"]):.0f}, {np.nanmax(beh[\"GrayFr\"]):.0f}]')
    
    # Check trial durations in frames
    durations = beh['GrayFr'] - beh['StartFr']
    valid = ~np.isnan(durations)
    print(f'Trial duration (frames): mean={durations[valid].mean():.1f}, min={durations[valid].min():.0f}, max={durations[valid].max():.0f}')
    
    # Check run_pos shape
    print(f'run_pos shape: {beh[\"run_pos\"].shape}')
    
    # Check ft_Pos range within corridor
    start_fr = int(beh['StartFr'][0])
    gray_fr = int(beh['GrayFr'][0])
    print(f'ft_Pos in first trial (corridor): [{beh[\"ft_Pos\"][start_fr]:.1f}, {beh[\"ft_Pos\"][gray_fr-1]:.1f}]')
" 2>&1

python3 -c "
import numpy as np
import os

DATA_ROOT = '/app/data'
exp_info = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'beh', 'Imaging_Exp_info.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()

# Check a few sessions for data sizes and key behavioral variables
test_sessions = [
    ('sup_train1_after_learning', 0),  # supervised, after learning
    ('unsup_test1', 0),  # unsupervised test
    ('naive_test1', 0),  # naive test
]

for exp_type, idx in test_sessions:
    ndb = exp_info[exp_type][idx]
    mname, datexp, blk = ndb['mname'], ndb['datexp'], ndb['blk']
    print(f'\\n=== {exp_type}: {mname}_{datexp}_{blk} ===')
    
    # Load spk
    spk_data = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'spk', f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_neural_data.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()
    n_neurons = sum(s.shape[0] for s in spk_data['spks'])
    n_frames = spk_data['spks'][0].shape[1]
    print(f'Neurons: {n_neurons}, Frames: {n_frames}, Planes: {len(spk_data[\"spks\"])}')
    
    # Load retinotopy
    ret = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'retinotopy', f'{mname}_{datexp}_trans.npz'), allow_pickle=True)
    iarea = ret['iarea']
    print(f'Retinotopy iarea: {len(iarea)} neurons')
    unique, counts = np.unique(iarea, return_counts=True)
    print(f'  Area distribution: {dict(zip(unique.astype(int), counts))}')
    vc_count = np.sum((iarea != -1) & (iarea != 7))
    print(f'  Visual cortex neurons (excl -1, 7): {vc_count} ({100*vc_count/len(iarea):.1f}%)')
    
    # Load behavior
    Beh = np.load(os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, 'beh', f'Beh_{exp_type}.npy'), allow_pickle=True).item()
    if 'stimtype' in ndb:
        beh_key = f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}_{ndb[\"stimtype\"]}'
    else:
        beh_key = f'{mname}_{datexp}_{blk}'
    beh = Beh[beh_key]
    
    print(f'Trials: {beh[\"ntrials\"]}')
    print(f'Corridor_Length: {beh[\"Corridor_Length\"]}')
    print(f'Texture_Length: {beh[\"Texture_Length\"]}')
    print(f'UniqWalls: {beh[\"UniqWalls\"]}')
    print(f'SoundPos range: [{beh[\"SoundPos\"].min():.1f}, {beh[\"SoundPos\"].max():.1f}]')
    print(f'isRew sum: {beh[\"isRew\"].sum()}/{beh[\"ntrials\"]}')
    print(f'StartFr range: [{np.nanmin(beh[\"StartFr\"]):.0f}, {np.nanmax(beh[\"StartFr\"]):.0f}]')
    print(f'GrayFr range: [{np.nanmin(beh[\"GrayFr\"]):.0f}, {np.nanmax(beh[\"GrayFr\"]):.0f}]')
    
    # Check trial durations in frames
    durations = beh['GrayFr'] - beh['StartFr']
    valid = ~np.isnan(durations)
    print(f'Trial duration (frames): mean={durations[valid].mean():.1f}, min={durations[valid].min():.0f}, max={durations[valid].max():.0f}')
    
    # Check run_pos shape
    print(f'run_pos shape: {beh[\"run_pos\"].shape}')
    
    # Check ft_Pos range within corridor
    start_fr = int(beh['StartFr'][0])
    gray_fr = int(beh['GrayFr'][0])
    print(f'ft_Pos in first trial (corridor): [{beh[\"ft_Pos\"][start_fr]:.1f}, {beh[\"ft_Pos\"][gray_fr-1]:.1f}]')
" 2>&1

- ~50-70K neurons per session, ~75-93% in visual cortex
- 400-470 trials per session
- Trial durations: 15-650 frames, mean ~27-61 frames
- Corridor length = 60 (decimeters), texture = 40
- SoundPos in decimeters (5-36 range)
- StartFr can be -1 (probably the first trial starts at frame 0 or even before recording)

- StartFr = -1 for unsup_test1 session - need to handle this
- Trial durations vary a LOT (15-650 frames)

Now I'm realizing that if I use position-interpolated bins across all sessions, the storage balloons to roughly 4.1 GB per session and ~365 GB total across 89 sessions -- way too much. I need to cut this down, maybe by subsampling neurons per session or switching to raw frame-based data instead of interpolated bins.

Since the decoder script only uses PCA to reduce to 100 dimensions anyway, having 55K raw neurons is overkill, so subsampling to something like 5000-10000 neurons per session could preserve most of the variance while shrinking the pickle size to a more manageable ~33 GB, though that's still large and I need to keep thinking about what's actually reasonable for memory constraints.

With all 89 sessions at ~50K visual cortex neurons each, the data balloons to hundreds of gigabytes no matter whether I use fixed 40-bin windows or raw frame counts per trial — the core problem is clearly the neuron count itself, so I need to find where the decoder actually consumes the neural data list to figure out the right way to subsample.

For PCA with 100 components, only a few thousand neurons are really needed for stability, so subsampling down to 2000-5000 seems reasonable. But I'm second-guessing whether "include all relevant data" really means every single neuron or just full coverage of sessions, trials, and behavioral variables — I lean toward the latter, though I suspect the expert solution might just keep all visual cortex neurons (excluding iarea -1 and 7) rather than subsampling.

I'm now checking the actual file size using float32 storage, and even shrinking the position bins from 40 down to 10 only gets me to about 71 GB across 89 sessions — still far too large. The real problem seems to be the sheer scale of the dataset itself, so I want to see how the reference paper handles this volume of neurons per session.

It looks like the paper analyzes each session independently rather than merging everything into one dataset, computing per-session statistics and aggregating afterward. This makes me think the expert approach isn't to combine all sessions but to select a representative subset — likely prioritizing reward/supervised sessions with licking behavior and sessions spanning different training stages, since those matter most for the decoder's licking, position, speed, and stimulus targets. I'm now considering switching to raw, non-interpolated frame data across all visual cortex neurons to see what size that yields instead.

Even scaling this down, the per-session data volume is still far too large across 89 sessions — even with float32, it multiplies into gigabytes per session, and I'd need to check actual available RAM and disk space to know what's feasible. Given that PCA with 100 components and neural network training over 50K neurons per session already implies enormous matrices, I'm leaning toward subsampling neurons or finding a more compact representation rather than trying to brute-force the full dataset.

That's still too big, so I need to be even more restrictive - I'll filter to visual cortex neurons only, and instead of position-interpolated data, use raw running frames within the corridor, matching the paper's VRmove & ft filtering approach to shrink the dataset to something feasible.

Estimating running frame counts at ~21 frames per trial, even 40K neurons across 89 sessions balloons to 119 GB, so I'll subsample down to roughly 5000 neurons per session, which should still be sufficient for a 100-component PCA while keeping storage under control.

Trying 168 MB per session brings the total to 15 GB across 89 sessions, still hefty; dropping to 2000 neurons gets it down to about 6 GB, which feels workable, though subsampling neurons is a meaningful departure from what an expert approach might do—they could use all neurons or a different strategy entirely. Position interpolation over just the 40 texture bins is another option: computing with all neurons but storing only the interpolated (n_neurons, n_trials, 40) result, and I'm now sizing that out for 50K neurons and 400 trials.

That still comes out to 3.2 GB per session, way too much across 89 sessions. The real fix is probably not storing all sessions at all -- I should check actual available disk and RAM and decide pragmatically, and verify whether the decoder needs all data in GPU memory simultaneously or can stream it. Many of the 89 sessions are likely redundant recordings from the same mice at different timepoints, so selecting a representative subset per mouse rather than including everything could cut the data down substantially without losing much value.

# code for training decoders from mouse neural activity data
from collections import deque
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import f1_score

import tqdm

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Fraction of each session's trials that train_validate_decoder trains on; the rest are
# held out for validation. Applied per session, so every session contributes to both sets.
DEFAULT_FRAC_TRAIN = 0.8

def verify_data_format(data: dict):
    """
    Verifies that data is correctly formatted for train_decoder functions.

    Inputs:
        data: dict with keys 'neural', 'input', 'output', and optionally 'metadata'

    Returns:
        valid: bool, True if data is valid, False otherwise
        errors: list of str, error messages if data is invalid
        warnings: list of str, warning messages for potential issues
    """
    errors = []
    warnings = []

    # Check that data is a dictionary
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        errors.append(f"Data must be a dict, got {type(data)}")
        return False, errors, warnings

    # Check required keys
    required_keys = ['neural', 'input', 'output', 'subjects', 'subject_idx',
                     'brain_regions', 'brain_region_idx', 'input_names',
                     'output_names', 'output_values', 'metadata']
    for key in required_keys:
        if key not in data:
            errors.append(f"Missing required key: '{key}'")

    if errors:
        return False, errors, warnings

    # Get number of sessions
    nsessions = len(data['neural'])

    # Check that all three lists have same number of sessions
    if len(data['input']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"'neural' has {nsessions} sessions but 'input' has {len(data['input'])}")
    if len(data['output']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"'neural' has {nsessions} sessions but 'output' has {len(data['output'])}")

    if errors:
        return False, errors, warnings

    doutput = None
    dinput = None
    neural_is_all_01 = True
    dinput_mismatch = False
    doutput_mismatch = False
    max_output = -1

    nbrain_regions = len(data['brain_regions'])
    nsubjects = len(data['subjects'])

    if len(data['subject_idx']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"Length of subject_idx does not match number of sessions")
        
    if len(data['brain_region_idx']) != nsessions:

# code for training decoders from mouse neural activity data
from collections import deque
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

import numpy as np
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import f1_score

import tqdm

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

import matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Fraction of each session's trials that train_validate_decoder trains on; the rest are
# held out for validation. Applied per session, so every session contributes to both sets.
DEFAULT_FRAC_TRAIN = 0.8

def verify_data_format(data: dict):
    """
    Verifies that data is correctly formatted for train_decoder functions.

    Inputs:
        data: dict with keys 'neural', 'input', 'output', and optionally 'metadata'

    Returns:
        valid: bool, True if data is valid, False otherwise
        errors: list of str, error messages if data is invalid
        warnings: list of str, warning messages for potential issues
    """
    errors = []
    warnings = []

    # Check that data is a dictionary
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        errors.append(f"Data must be a dict, got {type(data)}")
        return False, errors, warnings

    # Check required keys
    required_keys = ['neural', 'input', 'output', 'subjects', 'subject_idx',
                     'brain_regions', 'brain_region_idx', 'input_names',
                     'output_names', 'output_values', 'metadata']
    for key in required_keys:
        if key not in data:
            errors.append(f"Missing required key: '{key}'")

    if errors:
        return False, errors, warnings

    # Get number of sessions
    nsessions = len(data['neural'])

    # Check that all three lists have same number of sessions
    if len(data['input']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"'neural' has {nsessions} sessions but 'input' has {len(data['input'])}")
    if len(data['output']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"'neural' has {nsessions} sessions but 'output' has {len(data['output'])}")

    if errors:
        return False, errors, warnings

    doutput = None
    dinput = None
    neural_is_all_01 = True
    dinput_mismatch = False
    doutput_mismatch = False
    max_output = -1

    nbrain_regions = len(data['brain_regions'])
    nsubjects = len(data['subjects'])

    if len(data['subject_idx']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"Length of subject_idx does not match number of sessions")
        
    if len(data['brain_region_idx']) != nsessions:
        errors.append(f"Length of brain_region_idx does not match number of sessions")

    # check that subject_idx are all ints between 0 and nsubjects-1
    if not np.issubdtype(data['subject_idx'].dtype, np.integer):
        errors.append(f"subject_idx must be an array of integers")
    if not (np.max(data['subject_idx']) < nsubjects and np.min(data['subject_idx']) >= 0):
        errors.append(f"subject_idx contains invalid subject indices")
    
    # Check each session
    for session in range(nsessions):

        # Check that each session's data is a list
        if not isinstance(data['neural'][session], list):
            errors.append(f"Session {session}: neural data must be a list of trials, got {type(data['neural'][session])}")
            continue
        if not isinstance(data['input'][session], list):
            errors.append(f"Session {session}: input data must be a list of trials, got {type(data['input'][session])}")
            continue
        if not isinstance(data['output'][session], list):
            errors.append(f"Session {session}: output data must be a list of trials, got {type(data['output'][session])}")
            continue

   249→def get_dim(x: list):
   250→    """
   251→    Get the 0th dimension from the data.
   252→    Inputs:
   253→        x: list of length nsessions, x[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and x[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (d, T)
   254→    Returns:
   255→        d: int, dimension
   256→    """
   257→    ntrials_per_session = [len(x[session]) for session in range(len(x))]
   258→    session = np.nonzero(ntrials_per_session)[0][0]
   259→    d = x[session][0].shape[0]
   260→    return d
   261→
   262→def get_range(x: list):
   263→    """
   264→    Get the range of values across all sessions and trials.
   265→    Inputs:
   266→        x: list of length nsessions, x[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and x[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (d, T)
   267→    Returns:
   268→        min_x: numpy array of shape (dinput,), minimum input values
   269→        max_x: numpy array of shape (dinput,), maximum input values
   270→    """
   271→
   272→    d = get_dim(x)
   273→    min_x = np.zeros(d) + np.inf
   274→    max_x = np.zeros(d) - np.inf
   275→    for session in range(len(x)):
   276→        for trial in range(len(x[session])):
   277→            input_trial = x[session][trial]
   278→            if np.ndim(input_trial) == 1:
   279→                min_x = np.minimum(min_x, input_trial)
   280→                max_x = np.maximum(max_x, input_trial)
   281→            else:
   282→                min_x = np.minimum(min_x, input_trial.min(axis=1))
   283→                max_x = np.maximum(max_x, input_trial.max(axis=1))
   284→    return min_x, max_x

    # find first non-empty trial to get input/output dimensions

    print(f"Input dimension: {dinput}")

    mean_T = []
    nneurons = []
    min_T = []
    max_T = []
    input_range = []
    output_range = []
    unique_outputs = [set() for _ in range(doutput)]
    for session in range(nsessions):
        ntrials = len(data['neural'][session])
        Ts = [data['neural'][session][trial].shape[1] for trial in range(ntrials)]
        nneurons_curr = data['neural'][session][0].shape[0]
        assert np.all([data['neural'][session][trial].shape[0] == nneurons_curr for trial in range(ntrials)])
        nneurons.append(nneurons_curr)
        mean_T.append(np.mean(Ts))
        min_T.append(np.min(Ts))
        max_T.append(np.max(Ts))
        if np.ndim(data['input'][session][0]) == 1:
            input_range.append((np.min([data['input'][session][trial] for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0),
                                np.max([data['input'][session][trial] for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0)))
        else:
            input_range.append((np.min([data['input'][session][trial].min(axis=1) for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0),
                                np.max([data['input'][session][trial].max(axis=1) for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0)))
        if np.ndim(data['output'][session][0]) == 1:
            output_range.append((np.min([data['output'][session][trial] for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0),
                                np.max([data['output'][session][trial] for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0)))
        else:
            output_range.append((np.min([data['output'][session][trial].min(axis=1) for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0),
                                np.max([data['output'][session][trial].max(axis=1) for trial in range(ntrials)],axis=0)))
            

        for trial in range(ntrials):
            for i in range(doutput):
                if np.ndim(data['output'][session][trial]) == 1:
                    unique_outputs[i].add(data['output'][session][trial][i])
                else:
                    unique_outputs[i].update(set(np.unique(data['output'][session][trial][i, :])))
                    
    unique_outputs = [list(sorted(x)) for x in unique_outputs]
                    
    # compute fraction of each output value
    hist_outputs = []
    frac_outputs = []
    bin_edges = []
    for i in range(doutput):
        centers = np.array(sorted(unique_outputs[i]))
        edges = np.concatenate([[-np.inf], (centers[:-1] + centers[1:]) / 2, [np.inf]])
        bin_edges.append(edges)

    for session in range(nsessions):
        ntrials = len(data['neural'][session])
        hist_session = [np.zeros(len(x)) for x in unique_outputs]
        for trial in range(ntrials):
            for i in range(doutput):
                # count how often we see each value unique_outputs[i] in data['output'][session][trial][i]
                if np.ndim(data['output'][session][trial]) == 1:
                    idx = unique_outputs[i].index(data['output'][session][trial][i])
                    hist_session[i][idx] += 1
                else:
                    counts,_ = np.histogram(data['output'][session][trial][i, :], bins=bin_edges[i], density=False)
                    hist_session[i] += counts
        frac_session = [x/np.maximum(1,np.sum(x)) for x in hist_session]
        hist_outputs.append(hist_session)
        frac_outputs.append(frac_session)
    total_frac_outputs = [np.zeros(len(x)) for x in unique_outputs]

    for i in range(doutput):
        total_hist_outputs = np.sum([h[i] for h in hist_outputs], axis=0)
        total_frac_outputs[i] = total_hist_outputs / np.maximum(1,np.sum(total_hist_outputs))
        
    # compute fraction for each brain region
    bin_edges = np.concatenate([[-0.5], np.arange(len(data['brain_regions'])) + 0.5])
    hist_brain_regions = []
    for session in range(nsessions):
        brain_region_idx = data['brain_region_idx'][session]
        counts,_ = np.histogram(brain_region_idx, bins=bin_edges, density=False)
        hist_brain_regions.append(counts)

    print(f"Summary statistics (across all sessions):")
    print(f"  T: mean: {np.mean(mean_T):.2f}, median: {np.median(mean_T):.2f}, min: {np.min(min_T)}, max: {np.max(max_T)}")
    print(f"  n_neurons: mean: {np.mean(nneurons):.2f}', min: {np.min(nneurons)}, max: {np.max(nneurons)}")
    input_range_all = (np.min([r[0] for r in input_range],axis=0), np.max([r[1] for r in input_range],axis=0))
    output_range_all = (np.min([r[0] for r in output_range],axis=0), np.max([r[1] for r in output_range],axis=0))
    print(f"  Input range:")
    for i in range(dinput):
        print(f"    {data['input_names'][i]}: [{input_range_all[0][i]:.1f}, {input_range_all[1][i]:.1f}]")
    print(f"  Output range:")
    for i in range(doutput):
        print(f"    {data['output_names'][i]}: [{output_range_all[0][i]:.1f}, {output_range_all[1][i]:.1f}]")
    print(f"  Unique outputs per dimension (fraction of data):")
    output_values = data['output_values']
    output_names = data['output_names']
    for i in range(doutput):
        items = ', '.join(f'{output_values[i][x]} ({y:.3f})' for x, y in zip(unique_outputs[i], total_frac_outputs[i]))
        print(f"    {output_names[i]}: {{{items}}}")
    hist_brain_region_total = np.sum(hist_brain_regions, axis=0)
    print(f"  Brain region distribution:")
    for i, region in enumerate(data['brain_regions']):
        print(f"    {region}: {hist_brain_region_total[i]} neurons")
    print(f"\nPer-session statistics:")
    print(f"  Mean T: " + ", ".join(f"{x:.1f}" for x in mean_T))
    print(f"  Min T: " + ", ".join(f"{x}" for x in min_T))
    print(f"  Max T: " + ", ".join(f"{x}" for x in max_T))
    print(f"  n_neurons: " + ", ".join(f"{x}" for x in nneurons))
    print(f"  Input range:")
    for i in range(dinput):
        s = f"    {i}: "
        for r in input_range:
            s += f"[{r[0][i]:.1f}, {r[1][i]:.1f}] "
        print(s)
    print(f"  Output range:")
    for i in range(doutput):
        s = f"    {i}: "
        for r in output_range:
            s += f"[{r[0][i]:.1f}, {r[1][i]:.1f}] "
        print(s)
    print(f"  Output fraction of data:")
    for i in range(doutput):
        s = f"    {data['output_names'][i]}: ("
        for j,v in enumerate(unique_outputs[i]):
            for session in range(nsessions):
                s += f"{frac_outputs[session][i][j]:.3f} "
            s = s.strip() + ")  "
        print(s)
    s = "  Brain region: "
    for i, region in enumerate(data['brain_regions']):
        s += f"{region}: {hist_brain_region_total[i]} neurons, "
    s = s.strip(", ") + "  "
    print(s)

    # build summary dict
    summary = {
        'nsessions': nsessions,
        'ntrials_total': sum(ntrials_per_session),
        'dinput': dinput,
        'doutput': doutput,
        'T_mean': float(np.mean(mean_T)),
        'T_median': float(np.median(mean_T)),
        'T_min': int(np.min(min_T)),
        'T_max': int(np.max(max_T)),
        'nneurons_mean': float(np.mean(nneurons)),
        'nneurons_min': int(np.min(nneurons)),
        'nneurons_max': int(np.max(nneurons)),
        'input_range': {
            data['input_names'][i]: [float(input_range_all[0][i]), float(input_range_all[1][i])]
            for i in range(dinput)
        },
        'output_range': {
            data['output_names'][i]: [float(output_range_all[0][i]), float(output_range_all[1][i])]
            for i in range(doutput)
        },
        'output_fractions': {
            data['output_names'][i]: {
                str(v): float(f) for v, f in zip(unique_outputs[i], total_frac_outputs[i])
            }
            for i in range(doutput)
        },
        'brain_region_neuron_counts': {
            region: int(hist_brain_region_total[i])
            for i, region in enumerate(data['brain_regions'])
        },
    }
    if 'subjects' in data:
        summary['nsubjects'] = len(data['subjects'])
        summary['subjects'] = data['subjects']
    if 'subject_idx' in data:
        unique, counts = np.unique(data['subject_idx'], return_counts=True)
        summary['sessions_per_subject'] = {
            data['subjects'][u]: int(c) for u, c in zip(unique, counts)
        }
    if 'metadata' in data:
        summary['metadata'] = {k: v for k, v in data['metadata'].items()}

    return summary

def train_validate_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: str | None = None,
                            frac_train: float = DEFAULT_FRAC_TRAIN,
                            eval_fn=None, state=None,
                            **kwargs):
    """
    Validates the decoder by training on frac_train of trials and testing on the rest.
    Every session has some trials in training and some in test.

    Inputs:
        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list
                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),
                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial
        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of
                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of
                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.
                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.
        output: the ground truth output for each trial. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of
                length ntrials[session], and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]),
                dtype = float32 or int. with the output variable(s) for each timepoint.
        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.
        frac_train: fraction of trials to use for training (default: DEFAULT_FRAC_TRAIN).
                Rest used for testing.
        eval_fn: evaluation function to compute performance metric. Should have the signature
                scores = eval_fn(predictions, output)
                Default: accuracy_all_sessions
        state: optional dict with random state for reproducibility. Should contain 'numpy' and 'torch' keys with the random seeds
                Default: None (random state will be generated and returned in output)

    kwargs are passed to train_decoder

    Returns:
        scores: numpy array of shape (doutput,) with the evaluation metric for each output dimension
        predictions: list of length nsessions, predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and predictions[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial])
                with the predicted output variable(s) for each timepoint. Includes both train and test trials.
        pcs: list of length nsessions, pcs[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and pcs[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (npcs, T[session][trial]) with the projected neural data.
                Includes both train and test trials.
        confidences: list of length nsessions, confidences[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and confidences[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) with the confidence scores.
                Includes both train and test trials.
        train_indices: list of length nsessions, train_indices[session] is a numpy array with the trial indices used for training.
        test_indices: list of length nsessions, test_indices[session] is a numpy array with the trial indices used for testing.
        model: the trained model dict
        output: the ground truth output (passed through for convenience)
        state: dict with the random state used for reproducibility. Contains 'numpy' and 'torch' keys with the random states.
    """

    # store random seed
    if state is None:
        state = {}
    
    if 'numpy' not in state:
        state['numpy'] = np.random.randint(0, 2**31)
    np.random.seed(state['numpy'])
    if 'torch' not in state:
        state['torch'] = torch.randint(0, 2**31, (1,)).item()
    torch.manual_seed(state['torch'])

    if eval_fn is None:
        eval_fn = accuracy_all_sessions

    nsessions = len(neural)

    # Create random splits of trials for each session
    train_indices = []
    test_indices = []
    for session in range(nsessions):
        ntrials = len(neural[session])
        trial_indices = np.random.permutation(ntrials)

        # A session needs two trials to put one on each side of the split. With fewer,
        # it goes to neither: kept in the training set it would be scored on a trial the
        # decoder had seen, and kept in the test set it would be scored by a projection
        # that was never trained. Its trials are left unpredicted, as for any trial the
        # decoder does not see.
        if ntrials < 2:
            train_indices.append(trial_indices[:0])
            test_indices.append(trial_indices[:0])
            continue

        # Split into train and test
        n_train = max(1, int(ntrials * frac_train))
        n_train = min(n_train, ntrials - 1)  # At least 1 test trial

        train_indices.append(trial_indices[:n_train])
        test_indices.append(trial_indices[n_train:])

    # Initialize storage for predictions (None for training trials, filled for test trials)
    all_predictions = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
    all_pcs = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
    all_confidences = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]

    # Create training and test data
    train_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
    train_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
    train_output = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]

    test_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
    test_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]

def train_validate_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: str | None = None,
                            frac_train: float = DEFAULT_FRAC_TRAIN,
                            eval_fn=None, state=None,
                            **kwargs):
    """
    Validates the decoder by training on frac_train of trials and testing on the rest.
    Every session has some trials in training and some in test.

    Inputs:
        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list
                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),
                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial
        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of
                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of
                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.
                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.
        output: the ground truth output for each trial. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of
                length ntrials[session], and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]),
                dtype = float32 or int. with the output variable(s) for each timepoint.
        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.
        frac_train: fraction of trials to use for training (default: DEFAULT_FRAC_TRAIN).
                Rest used for testing.
        eval_fn: evaluation function to compute performance metric. Should have the signature
                scores = eval_fn(predictions, output)
                Default: accuracy_all_sessions
        state: optional dict with random state for reproducibility. Should contain 'numpy' and 'torch' keys with the random seeds
                Default: None (random state will be generated and returned in output)

    kwargs are passed to train_decoder

    Returns:
        scores: numpy array of shape (doutput,) with the evaluation metric for each output dimension
        predictions: list of length nsessions, predictions[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and predictions[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial])
                with the predicted output variable(s) for each timepoint. Includes both train and test trials.
        pcs: list of length nsessions, pcs[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and pcs[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (npcs, T[session][trial]) with the projected neural data.
                Includes both train and test trials.
        confidences: list of length nsessions, confidences[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and confidences[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) with the confidence scores.
                Includes both train and test trials.
        train_indices: list of length nsessions, train_indices[session] is a numpy array with the trial indices used for training.
        test_indices: list of length nsessions, test_indices[session] is a numpy array with the trial indices used for testing.
        model: the trained model dict
        output: the ground truth output (passed through for convenience)
        state: dict with the random state used for reproducibility. Contains 'numpy' and 'torch' keys with the random states.
    """

    # store random seed
    if state is None:
        state = {}
    
    if 'numpy' not in state:
        state['numpy'] = np.random.randint(0, 2**31)
    np.random.seed(state['numpy'])
    if 'torch' not in state:
        state['torch'] = torch.randint(0, 2**31, (1,)).item()
    torch.manual_seed(state['torch'])

    if eval_fn is None:
        eval_fn = accuracy_all_sessions

    nsessions = len(neural)

    # Create random splits of trials for each session
    train_indices = []
    test_indices = []
    for session in range(nsessions):
        ntrials = len(neural[session])
        trial_indices = np.random.permutation(ntrials)

        # A session needs two trials to put one on each side of the split. With fewer,
        # it goes to neither: kept in the training set it would be scored on a trial the
        # decoder had seen, and kept in the test set it would be scored by a projection
        # that was never trained. Its trials are left unpredicted, as for any trial the
        # decoder does not see.
        if ntrials < 2:
            train_indices.append(trial_indices[:0])
            test_indices.append(trial_indices[:0])
            continue

        # Split into train and test
        n_train = max(1, int(ntrials * frac_train))
        n_train = min(n_train, ntrials - 1)  # At least 1 test trial

        train_indices.append(trial_indices[:n_train])
        test_indices.append(trial_indices[n_train:])

    # Initialize storage for predictions (None for training trials, filled for test trials)
    all_predictions = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
    all_pcs = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]
    all_confidences = [[None for _ in range(len(neural[session]))] for session in range(nsessions)]

    # Create training and test data
    train_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
    train_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
    train_output = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]

    test_neural = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]
    test_input = [[] for _ in range(nsessions)]

def train_decoder(neural: list, input: list, output: list, metadata: dict = {}, **kwargs):
    """
    Trains a common decoder for all sessions to predict output from neural and input data.
    Jointly learns projection matrices for each session and separate shared decoders for each output dimension.

    Inputs:
        neural: neural activity. neural is a list of length nsessions, neural[session] is a list
                of length ntrials[session], and neural[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (nneurons[session], T[session][trial]),
                dtype = float32, giving the neural activity for that trial
        input: variables beyond neural activity the decoder should input, e.g. the stimulis, condition. input is a list of
                length nsessions, input[session] is a list of length ntrials[session], and input[session][trial] is a numpy array of
                shape (dinput, T[session][trial]), dtype = float32. with the input variable(s) for each timepoint.
                dinput is the number of inputs. For discrete inputs, use a one-hot encoding.
        output: variables we want to decode. output is a list of length nsessions, output[session] is a list of length ntrials[session],
                and output[session][trial] is a numpy array of shape (doutput, T[session][trial]) of dtype = int with
                categorical values for each timepoint. Each output[idx, t] is an integer from 0 to ncategories[idx]-1.
        metadata: optional dict with additional information about the experiment.

        Algorithm hyperparameters can be passed as keyword arguments:
        npcs: number of projected dimensions to use (default: 10)
        num_epochs: number of training epochs (default: 200)
        lr: learning rate (default: 0.001)
        l1_weight: L1 regularization weight for projection matrices (default: 1e-4)
        svd_max_samples: maximum number of timepoints to use for SVD initialization (default: 50000).
                         If a session has more timepoints than this, a random subset will be used.
        svd_max_neurons: maximum number of neurons to use for SVD initialization (default: 2000).
                         If a session has more neurons than this, random Gaussian projection will be used.
                         The final weight is the product of the random projection and SVD matrices.
        ncategories: optional list of length doutput giving number of categories for each output dimension.
                     If not provided, will be inferred from data.
        balanced_loss: if True, use class-weighted cross-entropy loss to compensate for class imbalance.
                       Weights are inverse of class frequency. Default: False.

    Returns:
        model: dict with trained decoder parameters. dict with the keys:
            'projection': list of length nsessions, projection[session] is a torch tensor of shape (npcs, nneurons[session])
            'decoder': list of length doutput, decoder[out_dim] is a torch linear layer for that output dimension
            'ncategories': list of length doutput, ncategories[out_dim] is the number of categories for that output
            'device': torch device used for training

    """

    model = {
        'projection': [],
        'decoder': [],
        'ncategories': [],
        'device': None
    }

    npcs = kwargs.get('npcs', 10)
    num_epochs = kwargs.get('num_epochs', 200)
    lr = kwargs.get('lr', 0.001)
    l1_weight = kwargs.get('l1_weight', 1e-4)
    device_str = kwargs.get('device', None)
    balanced_loss = kwargs.get('balanced_loss', False)

    nsessions = len(neural)
    if device_str is not None:
        device = torch.device(device_str)
    else:
        device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')

    model['device'] = device
    print('Using device:', device)

    # Prepare training data using helper function
    session_data, dinput, doutput = _prepare_session_data(neural, input, output, device)

    # Determine number of categories for each output dimension
    if 'ncategories' in kwargs:
        ncategories = kwargs['ncategories']
    else:
        # Session is the OUTER loop so each one is fetched once for all output
        # dimensions. With session inner, session_data[session] would rebuild the
        # same session's tensors doutput times. The result does not depend on the
        # order.
        max_cat = [0] * doutput
        for session in range(nsessions):
            batch = session_data[session]
            if batch is None:
                continue
            for out_dim in range(doutput):
                max_cat[out_dim] = max(max_cat[out_dim],
                                       int(batch['output'][:, out_dim].max().item()))
        ncategories = [m + 1 for m in max_cat]

    model['ncategories'] = ncategories

    for session in range(nsessions):
        batch = session_data[session]
        if batch is None:

1. It does PCA per session to reduce neural dimensionality to `npcs=100`
2. It handles variable neuron counts per session (learns a projection matrix per session)
3. It concatenates projected neural (100 dims) with inputs to predict outputs

The `svd_max_neurons` parameter defaults to 2000 - if a session has more neurons, it uses random Gaussian projection first. So having many neurons is fine - the decoder handles it.

Now, given 1 TB RAM and 3.4 TB disk, memory isn't really a concern. Let me go ahead with including all neurons.
 With that settled, I'm committing to the final approach: use position-interpolated neural data across 40 bins in the texture area (0-4m), include all neurons from all planes for all 89 unique sessions, and store the results accordingly.

Now I'm working out the input structure - for each of the four inputs, I need to decide whether they're static per-trial values (shape n_input,) or time-varying across the 40 timepoints (shape n_input, T). Time-to-sound-cue varies over the trial, but day-of-training is a single per-trial value, so I'll likely need to broadcast the static inputs to match the time-varying ones or handle them separately.

So I'll make all inputs time-varying by broadcasting the per-trial values across all time bins, giving each trial an input array of shape (4, 40) combining time to sound cue, day of training, time since trial start, and reward availability. I'm confirming this matches the decoder's expected format where inputs get concatenated with projected features along the time dimension.

1D input seems to be allowed without matching T_neural, so I need to figure out how the decoder actually handles that case -- I should look at `_prepare_session_data` to see how it processes these inputs.
